liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hard To Handle** (2 reviews): Listener loves this song, especially with Pigpen performing it; Described as a really muscular performance, serving as the show's highlight [5][7]
- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Drumming is slightly offbeat before the band charges into a circular sound; Good Lovin' and the subsequent jam sequence are absolute masterpieces in energy [7][13]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-10-23.aud.wolfson.motb-0004.85071.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 27 songs; 137 min; rated 4.38/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Bass and drums are clear with little distortion, and vocals are distinct; The band is easily heard, though cymbal technique is not fully captured; Much clearer than another source, lacking muddiness in the middle frequencies [3][4][9][13]
- **gd1970-10-23.aud-wolfson.sketchy-bontempo.12227.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 112 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: The sound seems muddied to the listener, who is new to the archive [12]

## Around the show

- Audience talking during this song makes the recording feel immersive [5]
- Reviewer attended at age 18, having first seen the Dead in April 1970 [11]
- Listener thanks Gary Wolfson and Lydia for bringing the show to life [14]
- Opened with Casey Jones and closed with Uncle John's Band, reversing album order [6]
- NRPS performance was poor, but the Dead's sets are golden recordings [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-10-23.aud.wolfson.motb-0004.85071.flac16**: taped by Cary Wolfson; transferred by D. McCabe; source: Audience by Cary Wolfson AUD > Sony TC-124 > MAC [1]
- **gd1970-10-23.aud-wolfson.sketchy-bontempo.12227.shnf**: taped by Cary Wolfson; transferred by sketchybontempo; source: Sony TC124 with a 1 point stereo mic 15 feet back from stage [2]. Also: Uncertainty exists on whether Me & My Uncle was played before or after Good Lovin' [2]
